title: Laser Lords (Europe)
symptom: Gameplay and menu scenes appear vertically compressed with prominent horizontal letterboxing compared with their expected 4:3 presentation
expected: The title uses the hardware-selected PAL raster and compatibility mode without unintended vertical compression or frontend-added letterboxing

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: Laser Lords intentionally selects the PAL 625-line compatibility picture, yielding a centered 720x480 active image within the larger PAL raster. The visible horizontal bars would therefore be authored hardware output rather than frontend letterboxing.
supporting_evidence: The MCD212 specification defines a 625 compatibility mode with a centered 720x480 picture and vertical masking.
Both screenshots show coherent complete scenes rather than damaged line decoding.
The disc contains separate PAL and NTSC bumper assets, demonstrating deliberate standard-specific authoring.
contradicting_evidence: The user reports that the picture also appears vertically squashed, which may indicate incorrect presentation rather than intentional masking.
No real-hardware Laser Lords Europe capture or live CF/ST trace has yet confirmed the selected mode.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Trace CF, ST, FD, SM, field parity, DCA start lines, and core DisplayGeometry during both submitted scenes. A standard 625 mode request with no compatibility mask would falsify the authored-compatibility explanation.
citations: MCD212 Technical Specification tables 5-1 through 5-7 and section 5.8
Green Book V.2.2, V.2.3, and V.4.8

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The emulator misinterprets the title's MCD212 CF/ST/FD/SM state or applies PAL compatibility masking to a standard-mode picture, reducing the active vertical extent and producing unintended bars.
supporting_evidence: The reported distortion affects unrelated menu and gameplay scenes consistently.
Historical PAL/NTSC framing reports identify MCD212 mode interpretation as an unresolved shared dependency.
contradicting_evidence: Existing table-driven DisplayGeometry tests cover the documented PAL standard and compatibility apertures.
The screenshots may be exactly consistent with intentional PAL compatibility output.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Record the guest-programmed MCD212 mode and compare the resulting geometry and masked-line fetch behavior with the specification tables. If the traced mode, mask, and aperture match the documented 625 compatibility case, this emulator-decoding hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The frontend applies the wrong PAL pixel-aspect or treats a 480-line compatibility picture as though its content fills all 560 picture rows, making correctly masked guest output look vertically compressed.
supporting_evidence: The user perceives both letterboxing and vertical squashing in the final saved presentation.
contradicting_evidence: Screenshots, window aspect, and mouse mapping share the same core-provided DisplayGeometry.
Other PAL titles have been manually reported as correctly proportioned on the same build.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare one captured core raster with frontend output, then verify the pixel-aspect calculation against the traced geometry. Identical content proportions at both stages falsify a frontend-only cause.
citations: Philips TN 093 image-format and safe-area guidance

manual_verification.notes: User supplied two Laser Lords Europe screenshots showing prominent horizontal bars and perceived vertical compression in distinct menu/gameplay scenes. The report is current, but correctness versus authored PAL compatibility mode remains unclassified.
This incident tracks vertical geometry only. Laser Lords USA and Kether bottom-row corruption remain separate display-provenance incidents.
